articles.description:
The Problem: What is JWT Security?


JWT Security is the practice of safely using JSON Web Tokens (JWTs), a compact method for securely transmitting data between systems, to manage user authentication and authorization without constantly checking a database. You've encountered this problem if you've ever built a modern web API, a single-page application, or a mobile app backend and needed a way to keep users logged in across multiple requests after their initial login—without storing session state on your server. It solves the headache of "How do I remember who this user is?" with every API call, but it introduces new risks if implemented carelessly.
Think of a JWT like a tamper-evident, self-service concert ticket. When you first buy the ticket (log in), the venue's system (your auth serv…

You think 1,000 concurrent users is easy? Most senior developers I've worked with would fail this challenge spectacularly. They'd reach for microservices, throw Redis at everything, and wonder why their beautifully architected system crumbles under load that a simple PHP script could handle.
The problem isn't lack of knowledge about distributed systems or fancy tools. It's that developers optimize for the wrong metrics and misunderstand what "concurrent" actually means.
Here's what kills me: developers obsess over theoretical throughput while ignoring the brutal reality of connection management. A single server can theoretically handle millions of requests per second, but most can't even maintain 1,000 persistent connections without choking.

articles.author: Neelima Dhingra
articles.description:
Rarely does anyone think about temples.
But if you look closely, temples operate like complex service organizations:
Multiple daily services
Fixed and dynamic pricing
High seasonal traffic
Inventory usage
Financial tracking
Customer (devotee) management
That’s essentially an operations-heavy environment.
So what happens when such an ecosystem runs entirely on manual processes?
Chaos.
The Operational Bottleneck
Let’s analyze the traditional workflow:
Devotee walks in.
Requests a pooja.
Staff checks a physical register.
Slot availability is manually verified.
Payment is collected.
Paper receipt is issued.
Details are recorded again somewhere else.
This system works — until scale increases.
During festivals or special occasions:
Bookings multiply.
Manual errors increase.
Staff workload spikes…
articles.title: From Chaos to Clarity: Turning Temple Operations into a Structured Digital System
